This is something that's irked me for a long time. You can call it a pet peeve. Mobile pages! ARUGH! I really, really, really, REALLY disliked them. I can understand the appeal when you're on a mobile device such as a tablet or cell phone, but in most instances if a mobile version of a page is available the server will redirect the browser to the mobile version. It seems to me that people submitting mobile links are just too flipping lazy to take the ".m" out of the URL, and then claim that it's "hard" to edit. It'll take them an extra 60 seconds! If you click on these links using an actual computer then you're presented with a screwed up, nigh unreadable, version of the page that's two inches wide and scrolls longer than artifacts found in the vicinity of the Dead Sea. Can we please just prohibit this behavior? I can't really think of any reason for allowing people to submit links to mobile pages, and it's highly aggravating to people using a proper browser. At the very least can the Voat developers consider parsing submissions for ".m" and removing the characters? I understand that may present other challenges (such as making sure the URL is valid), but it would go a long way towards ensuring that the site can present consistent content in spite of ID-10-T user errors.
